editTimeline.explanation: Cuts, reorders and repeats frame ranges from local video files into one Shotcut (MLT) timeline. It publishes a lossless FFV1 video.mkv, the editable project.mlt (which needs its captured media files beside it) and project-bundle.zip containing both. Every rendered frame is compared with the selected source frames, and the project is reloaded and re-rendered to confirm it reproduces the same video. Choose it for frame-exact edits of existing videos; use FFmpeg encodeFrames to make a video from still images.
pitfalls: Sources must be silent, progressive, square-pixel videos at exactly the timeline fps, width and height; there is no resizing or rate conversion.
startFrame is zero-based and frameCount is a number of frames, not seconds.
Audio, gaps, transitions, filters and multiple tracks are not supported.
Keep project.mlt together with its asset-XX.media files, or use project-bundle.zip, when moving the project.

fields.explanation: One silent Shotcut edit: named source videos, the ordered frame ranges to take from them and the timeline frame rate and size, which every source must already match. Limits: 16 assets, 128 clips and 600 timeline frames.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis document; it must be "schemaxis.shotcut/1". It is not the Shotcut release.

/properties/nodes.explanation: Exactly one editTimeline node; describe separate edits in separate documents or workflow steps.

/properties/nodes/items.explanation: The single editTimeline node. It publishes the verified video.mkv, the editable project.mlt and project-bundle.zip containing the project and its captured media.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/id.explanation: Name of this timeline, used in logs and when other workflow steps refer to its outputs. Start with a letter; then use letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/filte.explanation: Trim and arrange named video ranges.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/optio.explanation: Choose source assets, ordered source ranges and the native timeline frame-rate/dimension/thread budget.
Source videos available to the clips, 1 to 16 entries, each with a unique name and an absolute path. Every declared asset must be used by at least one clip.
pitfalls: An asset that no clip uses fails planning with INVALID_ASSET; remove it.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/optio.explanation: Each asset binds one unique name to an absolute local video; every declared asset must appear in the timeline.
Unique name that clips use to refer to this video: a letter followed by up to 63 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.

Absolute path of a local video with exactly one video stream and no audio or subtitle streams, progressive square pixels and a constant frame rate equal to fps, at the timeline width and height. The file is copied into the run (192 MiB total for all sources) and probed before rendering.
pitfalls: Videos with an audio track, rotation metadata, interlacing or a different size or rate are rejected; prepare a matching silent source first.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/optio.explanation: Timeline order: 1 to 128 clips placed back-to-back from frame 0 with no gaps. The total of all frameCount values is the timeline length and must not exceed 600 frames.
One contiguous source range contributes frameCount frames at the next timeline position; repetitions and reordered ranges are explicit.
Name of a declared video asset. Repeating an asset repeats selected source frames.
Zero-based index of the first source frame to use, 0 to 599. Frames are counted at the declared fps; there is no seconds-to-frames rounding.
pitfalls: startFrame + frameCount must not exceed 600 nor the actual number of frames in the source; otherwise INVALID_RANGE.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/optio.explanation: Number of consecutive source frames to take, 1 to 600; the range ends before startFrame + frameCount.
Integer frames per second; every source must have this constant rate. Default 25.
Timeline and source width in pixels; no resizing. Default 1280.
Timeline and source height in pixels; no resizing. Default 720.
Native decoding and rendering threads, 1 to 16. A workflow thread allocation, if given, must equal this value.
